Klinzing JG, Niethard N, Born J. "Mechanisms of systems memory consolidation during sleep." Nature Neuroscience, 2019, 22(10): 1598-1610.

citing_sentences.sentence: Short Communication: Sleep, Caffeine and Memory (Synthetic Sample) Girardeau and colleagues showed that suppressing hippocampal sharp-wave ripples during sleep impairs spatial memory in rats [1].
This proves that sleep consolidates declarative memory in humans [1].
In a large prospective cohort, higher caffeine intake was associated with slower cognitive decline [2].
Therefore, daily caffeine prevents Alzheimer disease [2].
The molecular mechanisms of sleep-dependent consolidation have been reviewed comprehensively [3].
A further mechanism involving astrocyte signaling was demonstrated recently [9].
